summary: Even with a median household income north of $231,000 a year, the median home price exceeds $2 million — a price-to-income ratio above 8.6, meaning housing here is a stretch even at the top of the income distribution. That tension defines Cupertino: it sits in the western Santa Clara Valley, pressed against the eastern slopes of the Santa Cruz Mountains, which means the western half of town tilts upward into oak-studded foothills with genuine ridge-top sunset views, while the eastern half flattens into the valley floor occupied by Apple's ring-shaped headquarters and the surrounding tech campus sprawl. This is emphatically a job center, not a bedroom community — you can change employers among several major tech firms without changing your commute. The tradeoff is that outside those campuses, the streetscape is largely low-slung strip malls and wide arterials like Stevens Creek Boulevard, giving the city a car-oriented grain despite its compact 11.3-square-mile footprint. Evening life is quiet-suburban; the outdoor payoff comes from proximity to trails in the adjacent foothills and open-space preserves rather than a walkable downtown. With roughly 9.5 hours of daily sunshine, mild year-round temperatures averaging 69°F during the day, and a 4.3% poverty rate, the surface metrics gleam — but median rent above $3,500 a month and that eight-figure home price make Cupertino less a place you choose for lifestyle and more a place whose economics choose you.
